answer: One identity stewards one registered historic vessel: the register files hull and key, and each hull passes its annual survey on the dry-dock ledge. The steward's log threads every repair and fee to that hull; a second claim on it is rejected, so one hull backs exactly one identity. Per fake: 4,900 units (4,000 vessel share, 600 survey and fees, 300 meadow-creek mooring) and 180 days afloat; 100 fakes: 490,000 units, 100 vessels, 18,000 days. Cheapest cheat: buying a ready vessel at 7,000 units, but the seller surrenders their own hull's anchor; a forged survey fails the surveyor-key check.
